newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, confined to range.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, confined to range.

text.p: Gold prices were stuck in a narrow range of Monday afternoon after short covering and some physical buying lifted them a couple of dollars above Friday's level.
But dealer said trading was thin. "The summer season is really setting in now. Many traders aren't at their desks and those that are have their minds elsehere," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $321.70 per ounce just up from the $321.35 morning setting and compared with $319.50 on Friday.
Last week it plumbed a recent low fix of $315.75, which was its lowest setting since December 11, 1985.
Comex's August futures contract was up just 60 cents at $322.80 shortly after the fixing in very light business.
Some physical demand and short covering raised gold prices on Monday morning, but there was no follow through in Europe and dealers said the market outlook remained uncertain.
A weaker Australian dollar brought forward selling from Australian miners which slowed any rally potential the market might have had in the Far East, dealers said.
Gold prices slumped to near 12-year lows on news that the Australian central bank had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves during the previous six months.
The move cleared out over 60 percent of its reserves, and shocked the gold industry as Australia is the world's third largest gold miner after South Africa and the U.S.
Mining share analysts said the plunge in the gold price meant more than half of western gold miners were losing money.

South Africa's gold mining industry and the National Union of Mineworkers earlier on Monday unveiled a productivity-linked wage deal which could save thousands of jobs threatened by the gold price meltdown.
The pioneering two-year package offers miners substantial wage increases in exchange for a quantum leap in productivity designed to lift national gold output by nearly 20 percent.
That would mean an increase 1997 gold production by 90 tonnes from last year's 495 tonnes, the lowest South African production since 1956.s
Platinum and palladium were narrowly mixed with the firmer down $2.50 at $403.00/$407.00 and the later up $0.50 at $167.00/$171.00.
Silver was down eight cents at $4.30/$4.32.
